metaData.title: The Age of Fatigue in NEVs: Before the War Ends, Boredom Arrives
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Based on extensive first-hand interviews, this article deeply analyzes how China's NEV industry has fallen into a trap of homogenization, price wars, and declining profits, noting that intelligent driving has failed to deliver differentiation and long-term competition has transformed the sector from a 'good business' into a 'tedious, grueling one.'
metaData.summary: Using Tesla's cancellation of the Model 2 as a starting point, the article systematically examines the predicament of China's NEV industry from 2024 to the present. Intelligent driving was once the core battleground for differentiation, but after massive R&D investments, automakers found consumers unwilling to pay for it—autonomy became standard equipment without premium pricing. The price war has persisted for three years, spreading from complete vehicles to sales and the supply chain, with stringent sales targets, dealer losses, and suppliers forced below cost. Industry subsidies have exceeded 1.5 trillion yuan, incubating a complete supply chain but failing to prevent overcapacity. Once technology became 'good enough,' NEVs transformed from a world-changing dream into a thin-margin grind. Drawing on extensive practitioner interviews and industry data (BYD's profit decline, Zhongsheng's losses, autonomous driving engineers changing careers), the article captures the industry's shift from entrepreneurial passion to weary resignation, maintaining a cautious outlook on future consolidation.

mainPoints.point: Intelligent driving failed to become a core differentiator for automakers.
mainPoints.explanation: Consumers prioritize price, space, and exterior design when purchasing vehicles, assigning low weight to autonomous driving—some even request 'without autonomy, 10,000–20,000 yuan cheaper'—rendering massive corporate investments unable to command premiums.

mainPoints.point: Price wars have transmitted from complete vehicles to the entire industry chain, compressing profits and elevating risks.
mainPoints.explanation: From sales staff subsidizing commissions out of pocket and dealerships cutting coffee costs, to suppliers enduring dozens of bidding rounds and annual price reductions, costs have been pushed to the limit while risks rise, plunging the industry into irrational competition.

mainPoints.point: Once technology became 'good enough,' NEVs ceased to be a good business.
mainPoints.explanation: Severe product homogenization has all models converging toward design templates; prolonged subsidies have bred overcapacity that proves difficult to liquidate, fundamentally challenging the industry's profit model—a transformation previously witnessed in television and aviation.

keyQuotes: They did it too well, and so it stopped being a good business.
Consumers choosing brands because of autonomous driving ultimately never happened.
In the past, price wars were like fighting a battle for a day—when dawn broke, order was restored. Now it's been three years.

relatedArticles.title: AI Quarterly Report 26Q1: OpenClaw, the OpenAI vs. Anthropic Showdown, and Self-Evolution | LatePost Podcast
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through an interview with Silicon Valley VC partner Henry Yin, this article provides an in-depth review of key AI trends in Q1 2026, focusing on the Agent paradigm shift triggered by OpenClaw, the product competition between OpenAI and Anthropic, and the profound evolution of AI self-evolution and the SaaS industry.

relatedArticles.title: In Conversation with DJI's Frank Wang: Seeking Truth, Finding Freedom, and Living a Story
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: In his first in-depth interview after a decade of silence, DJI founder Frank Wang reflects on his journey from a brash 'genius geek' to a mature leader, exploring core philosophies on management, organizational entropy reduction, and technological innovation.

relatedArticles.title: QuantumBit Exclusive Interview with Lou Tiancheng: AI is a Runaway Horse, and Harness is the Most Critical Skill of This Era
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Pony.ai CTO Lou Tiancheng elaborates on the core philosophy of the PonyWorld World Model 2.0: when AI driving capabilities surpass humans, the value of human data drops to zero, AI must become the 'head coach' leading R&D, and the ability to harness this 'runaway horse' of AI will be the most critical skill of this era.

relatedArticles.title: A Comprehensive Guide to Microsoft Build 2026: The 'Agent-First' Era Arrives with Seven In-House Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Microsoft Build 2026 unveiled seven in-house MAI models, the Scout agent, the MXC system-level security sandbox, and Project Solara, marking the full implementation of an 'Agent-First' strategy.

relatedArticles.title: Dialogue with Minglue's Wu Minghui: AI is Killing SaaS, But I Found a New Path
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Wu Minghui, founder of Minglue Technology, believes that AI Agents will replace traditional SaaS, with the value of software itself approaching zero. The future business model will be open-source software combined with AI models and services, and he shares the practice and insights of his multi-Agent collaborative office platform 'Octopus'.

relatedArticles.title: "Wuzhao" Hasn't Changed, But AI Has Reshaped the Power Dynamic Between Companies and Talent
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Using the case of DingTalk CEO Chen Hang (Wuzhao) being directly replaced by Alibaba's Partnership Committee due to his high-pressure management style, this article delves into the fundamental shift in the power dynamic between large corporations and top talent in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: A Conversation with Lee Kai-Fu: Don't Call Us 'Six Little Tigers,' Call Us 'Leopards'
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: In an in-depth interview, 01.AI founder Lee Kai-Fu reveals that after abandoning pre-training large models, the company pivoted to To B enterprise AI transformation services, achieving 250 million RMB in revenue in 2025 and over 1.5 billion RMB in orders for 2026. The company is preparing for an IPO and hopes to be called 'Leopards' rather than 'Six Little Tigers.'

relatedArticles.title: 77. On the Vision and Ambition of Zhiyuan and MiFeng, and the Race in Embodied Intelligence | A Conversation with Yao Maoqing
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Zhiyuan partner Yao Maoqing deeply analyzes the reality that embodied intelligence is far from the 'GPT-1' moment, revealing Zhiyuan's full-stack strategy from hardware to data, and the strategic intent behind incubating the independent data platform 'MiFeng' from scratch.

relatedArticles.title: 143. Second Interview with He Xiaopeng: Bigger Bets, the Birth of Humanoid Robot Iron, the Unexpected Turn, CEO Under Technological Upheaval, GX, and the Stitch Monster
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: XPeng Motors Chairman He Xiaopeng shares in-depth insights into the company's strategic transformation from a smart EV company to a physical AI enterprise, including abandoning the old autonomous driving system, betting on the humanoid robot Iron, and the anxiety and decision-making amidst technological upheaval.

relatedArticles.title: Li Xiang × Luo Yonghao! Li Xiang's Ideal: Using AI Technology to Give Ordinary People a Life of Luxury
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Li Auto founder Li Xiang delves into the company's strategic logic for transforming from an automaker into an AI and embodied intelligence company, technical breakthroughs in self-developed chips and full-by-wire chassis, and his predictions for the endgame of autonomous driving and humanoid robots.
